preconditions.description: The number of employees (n) and events (m) are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= t <= 3 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for t in [int(line.split()[0])])
preconditions.description: Each event type (t) is either 1 (boss assignment), 2 (document packet), or 3 (query).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 1 for x, y in [(int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2]))])
preconditions.description: For type 1 events, x and y are valid employee numbers, and x has no boss before assignment.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 2 for x in [int(line.split()[1])])
preconditions.description: For type 2 events, x is a valid employee number.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= i <= packet_count for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 3 for x, i in [(int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2]))])
preconditions.description: For type 3 events, x is a valid employee number and i is a valid packet number (1 ≤ i ≤ total packets given so far).
There is at least one query of type 3 in the input.
The boss hierarchy never contains cycles at any point in time.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line in ['YES', 'NO'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines() if int(stdin.splitlines()[stdin.splitlines().index(line) + 1].split()[0]) == 3 for line in stdin.splitlines() if int(line.split()[0]) == 3)
postconditions.description: For each query of type 3, the output is either 'YES' (employee x signed packet i) or 'NO' (employee x did not sign packet i).

postconditions.expression: all((x in packet_path(i) if int(line.split()[0]) == 2 else True) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, i in [(int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2]))] if int(line.split()[0]) == 3)
postconditions.description: For a query (x, i), the output is 'YES' if and only if employee x is in the path of packet i (i.e., x signed packet i).

invariants.expression: all(1 <= employee <= n for employee in range(1, n + 1))
invariants.description: Employee numbers are always in the range 1 to n.

invariants.expression: all(1 <= packet <= packet_count for packet in range(1, packet_count + 1))
invariants.description: Packet numbers are always in the range 1 to the total packets given so far.
